title: AgentGym: Evolving Large Language Model-based Agents across Diverse Environments
data_curation: AGENTGYM spans 14 environments and 89 task types across web navigation (WebArena, WebShop), text games (MAZE, Wordle), household (ALFWorld), embodied (SciWorld, BabyAI), digital games (TextCraft), tool use (Weather, Movie, Academia, Sheet, TodoList), and programming (BIRD-SQL). The authors collect 20,509 instructions, reusing originals for data-rich tasks (WebShop, ALFWorld) and expanding sparse ones via self-instruct and instruction evolution prompted with GPT-3.5/4-Turbo. A diverse, challenging 1,160-instruction subset forms the AGENTEVAL benchmark; the rest is the training pool. Trajectories are collected ReAct-style from SOTA models (e.g., GPT-4-Turbo) plus crowdsourced human annotations, then filtered by reward/correctness, yielding AGENTTRAJ (6,130 trajectories) and its extension AGENTTRAJ-L (14,485) used as the behavioral-cloning upper bound. All trajectories use a unified ReAct format with environment-specific reward or success-rate feedback.
curriculum: Two ordered stages: (1) Behavioral cloning (BC) on AGENTTRAJ (Ds) plus a general-domain chat dataset to give the Llama-2-Chat-7B base agent instruction-following and prior knowledge, maximizing log pi(tau|e,u); (2) AGENTEVOL evolution, iterating M=4 times between an exploration step (the current agent samples one trajectory per instruction over a larger instruction set than BC) and a learning step (reward-weighted fine-tuning). Crucially, each iteration merges newly sampled trajectories with the *initial* AGENTTRAJ (not the previous iteration's) to avoid drift/overfitting. The general-domain data is retained throughout. BC runs 3 epochs at lr 1e-5; evolution runs 1 epoch per iteration at the same lr. Ablations show performance improves with M but converges, and that merging with initial data is more stable than chaining previous-iteration data.
method: AGENTEVOL reframes RL as probabilistic inference to sidestep the instability and cost of standard on-policy RL across many long-horizon agent tasks. Using the Dayan-Hinton / MAPPO connection, the authors derive a variational lower bound on log P(O=1) and obtain a tractable update that decouples data collection from policy optimization: in the exploration step the frozen previous policy samples trajectories and the environment assigns binary rewards (r<1 mapped to 0); in the learning step the agent minimizes a reward-weighted negative log-likelihood, i.e., maximizes E[r(e,u,tau) log pi_theta(tau|e,u)], effectively up-weighting high-reward trajectories. This is an iterative self-improvement loop (akin to ReST/STaR) generalized across multiple environments rather than a single task. The paper also experiments with adding failed trajectories via DPO, but finds reward-weighted SFT superior in the multi-task setting.
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses the AGENTEVAL benchmark suite (1,160 instructions) with per-environment success rate or reward as the metric, plus interactive-round counts for efficiency. Main backbone is Llama-2-Chat-7B (also tested 13B and DeepSeek-Coder-1.3B), trained on 8x A100-80GB (full evolution ~20h). Baselines include GPT-3.5/4-Turbo, Claude-3, DeepSeek-Chat, Llama-2-Chat, AgentLM-7B/13B/70B, BCbase (AGENTTRAJ), and BClarge (AGENTTRAJ-L). AGENTEVOL surpasses BClarge and rivals GPT-4-Turbo on many tasks: WebShop 76.5 vs 73.5, ALFWorld 88.0 vs 83.0, BabyAI 82.7 vs 74.19, TextCraft 64.0 vs 60.0, Tool-Weather 70.0 vs 65.0, while also reducing interactive rounds. Closed-source SOTA still leads on some tasks (e.g., BIRD, SciWorld).
key_results: AGENTEVOL on Llama-2-Chat-7B beats the behavioral-cloning upper bound BClarge on WebShop (76.5 vs 73.5), ALFWorld (88.0 vs 83.0), BabyAI (82.7 vs 74.19), and TextCraft (64.0 vs 60.0), and matches or surpasses GPT-4-Turbo on several environments. Evolution runs 4 iterations, ~20 hours on 8x A100-80GB, with K=1 sample per instruction.
evolution_note: Building on the RL-as-inference tradition (Dayan-Hinton, MAPPO) and single-task self-improvement lines (ReST, STaR, Trial-and-Error), AgentGym is an early 2024 attempt to push LLM agent self-evolution beyond isolated environments toward multi-environment generalists, complementing behavioral-cloning agent-tuning works like AgentTuning/AgentOhana. It foreshadows the later surge of RL/post-training for generalist LLM agents and the need for unified, concurrent agent training platforms.
